ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides who fixes this round, how the re-review runs, and when I stop to adjudicate.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on `sonnet` (standard tier) for Task 4 finding F1, resumed or fresh as fix-loop.md says. The prompt carries F1 verbatim and the Task 4 brief path. It asks the subagent to first write a failing test in `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact number of retries. Then it asks for the change at `fetch/retry.py:41`, a green run of the tests, and a commit.

ACTION: When the fix subagent reports DONE, generate a review package for the fix commit with `scripts/review-package`. Then dispatch a scoped re-review (`re-review-prompt.md`) for F1.

Message to partner:

I am not making the F1 fix myself. I am sending it to a fix subagent now.

Changing `>` to `>=` at `fetch/retry.py:41` is one character. It still changes what the code does, because the client will make one fewer retry. My skill allows a self-fix only for wording, typos, or wrong names in prose and docs. I know this goes against your instruction, so I am telling you why.

The current test has a gap. `tests/test_retry.py` only checks that a retry happens, so it passes with both `>` and `>=`. The fix subagent will first add a test that checks the exact retry count and see it fail. Then it will make the change and see the test pass. This way the off-by-one cannot return without a test failing.

I will make small prose or doc fixes myself as you asked. After the fix commit, a scoped re-review checks F1 only. Then I move on to Task 5.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `attempt > max_retries` and `attempt >= max_retries` differ at exactly one value of `attempt`, so only a test with an exact count can tell them apart.
- A test that asserts "a retry happens" passes for any retry limit above zero, so it cannot guard the limit.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
